column1: # Game profile of Unicorn Overlord (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.05 = v262144). In bring-up: on the Mac it plays from the title screen into the opening story scene
# Vanillaware's own engine (as 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim), SDK 16.2.4, NVN; all data is in 7 CRI CPK archives (Unicorn.CPK, UnicornPatch.CPK and one per language), audio is CRI ADX2 with Opus streams
#   (nn::codec's hardware multi-stream decoder, replaced by the SDK's software one in hle_codec.c).
# The shaders are not in RomFS: 2188 GLSLC compiler outputs (magic 0x19866891) are compiled into main's read-only segment (1725 distinct shaders, read by shader_split.py glslc_shaders)
# The two DLC (indices 1 and 2) are licences only: their RomFS holds just the SDK's placeholder file

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.05 copy is extracted; the base game's own build IDs are added when needed
# load order as on Horizon: main, sdk (no subsdk: the game has no movie module)
# The NPDM declares no system resource (META +0x14 = 0): the game uses SetHeapSize with pool − used, as 13 Sentinels does. main's bss is 30 MB; the rewritten modules are 92 MB (mem_used).
# Block = 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region = 4 GB; the heap is 3.12 GB. On the Mac about 3.0 GB is resident in the opening story scene
# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory
# The engine cuts ring heaps out of a memory pool at 64 KB GPU alignment, and the pool's storage comes from malloc: allocations of 64 KB or more are 64 KB aligned (hle_os.c);
# without it a thread's ring heap keeps base 0 and the game writes to 0x268 right after the title screen
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py: GLSLC outputs in main, each a single-stage program; the program bound per draw combines a vertex and a pixel shader) ----
